evidence.output: PROBE-URL http://. accepted -> target=http://. hostHeader=. | http://./x accepted | http://- accepted | http://-.- accepted | http://a..b accepted hostHeader=a..b | http://_ accepted
evidence.intent_output: If 'a required ASCII host given as a name' means a DNS-style name (non-empty labels), Proxy.to should throw IllegalArgumentException for '.', '-', '-.-' and 'a..b'

findings.title: TargetUrl.isHostName accepts degenerate names: '.', '-', 'a..b'
findings.description: isHostName checks only the character set plus the numeric-last-label rule, so empty labels, a lone dot, and labels that start or end with '-' pass. FR-PROXY-001 and D-048 require 'a required ASCII host given as a name' and reject 'every other URL', but they never define what a valid name is. RFC 3986 reg-name allows these strings. The proxy then fails late (DNS error, then 502) instead of throwing at Proxy.to. The intent is ambiguous, so the reviewer could not confirm a defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the name grammar (for example, RFC 1123 labels: non-empty, at most 63 characters, no leading or trailing '-', with '_' allowed as a deliberate choice), reject empty labels apart from one trailing root dot, and add assertRejected cases to ProxyTargetUrlTest.

clean_code.description: In requestTarget, the guards !remainder.endsWith(query) and !remainderPath.startsWith("/") cannot be reached on any current dispatch path. The common-HTTP view always carries the raw query suffix and a remainder that starts with '/', and the WebSocket view is the decoded full path plus the same raw query. No test reaches either branch, so removing them would not fail any test. Only the originalPath.endsWith(remainderPath) guard does work. The javadoc also suggests that this guard handles WebSocket requests under stripPrefix, but a plain WS path is forwarded unstripped (see out_of_scope_observations).
The scheme-default-port rule "https".equals(scheme) ? 443 : 80 is written twice, once in parse and once in hostHeader. A private static defaultPort(scheme) would keep the two in step.

Proxy.java is now 1021 lines and mixes the public option API, the request pipeline (checks, request target, Host choice), the socket forwarder, response head parsing and nested stream classes. Moving Target into TargetUrl was a good extraction. requestTarget/backendHost could follow PathChecker into a small package-private 'BackendTarget' helper.

authority is no longer used for the Host header (hostHeader() replaced it) and now serves only Proxy.describe(). That is fine, but its javadoc should say it exists only for describe(), so that it is not reused by mistake as a Host value (it keeps a written default port such as ':80').

out_of_scope_observations: SEC-PROXY-002: a client-sent X-Forwarded-Host is forwarded next to the proxy's own one. Probe (in-memory, Host: gw.example + X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example) -> backend X-Forwarded-Host values [evil.example, gw.example]. With no Host, the client value alone would reach the backend, which conflicts with the literal FR-PROXY-004 AC-4 'no X-Forwarded-Host' once SEC-PROXY-002 lands. HeaderRules.REQUEST_NOT_FORWARDED does not list x-forwarded-host.

FR-PROXY-009: a WebSocket upgrade to an app.ws route that reaches a .stripPrefix(true) proxy with a plain path is forwarded unstripped as a plain GET. Probe: upgrade /api/orders/7 -> backend 'GET /api/orders/7 HTTP/1.1' (expected '/7', or hand-off to next()). The requestTarget guard covers only decoded != raw. The D-050 WebSocket hand-off is meant to remove this.
